description: Construct a canonical minimum vertex-cover certificate in a bounded bipartite graph using augmenting-path matching and alternating reachability.

source.title: MinimumVertexCover.h and DFSMatching.h
source.reference: KACTL graph algorithms, CC0 algorithm descriptions
source.theorem_reference: Kőnig's theorem: in bipartite graphs, minimum vertex-cover size equals maximum-matching size
source.algorithm_attribution: Clean-room bounded Kuhn matching, alternating-cover construction, and lexicographic certificate refinement; algorithm descriptions only.

input.adjacency_mask_range: nonnegative masks with bits only in [0,right_count)
input.graph: simple bipartite graph; each left row is a set of adjacent right vertices

output.encoding: minimum-cover vertex mask; bit i selects left vertex i, bit left_count+j selects right vertex j
output.canonical_tie_rule: Among all minimum covers, choose the lexicographically smallest membership vector in vertex_id_order, with 0 before 1.

workspace.meaning: Fixed adjacency rows, right-to-left matching, alternating-reachability state, forced membership states, bounded Kuhn recursion, and call-frame allowance.

contract.matching: Process left vertices and right neighbors in ascending ID order. Each left vertex starts a DFS augmenting-path search with a fresh right-visited set.
contract.cover_construction: Begin from unmatched left vertices and follow alternating reachability. The initial certificate is (left vertices not reached) union (reached right vertices); its size equals the maximum matching size.
contract.canonical_refinement: Process vertices in vertex_id_order. Tentatively exclude each vertex; keep it excluded exactly when a minimum cover of the matching-derived size remains feasible. Otherwise include it. This pins the smallest membership vector across ports.
contract.validation: Reject null, truncated, or trailing frames; out-of-range partition sizes; negative row masks; and row bits outside the right partition.

oracle_method: The primary uses ordered augmenting-path matching, alternating reachability, and matching-feasibility refinement. The independent reference enumerates every vertex subset, checks edge coverage, then selects the minimum-cardinality cover with the specified lexicographic membership tie rule.
